assessment.why: This was only a warning; the detector did not pause the print. Over three frames spanning about 2 minutes, the strands at the small block and the strand running to the bed edge did not change at all. That means they are leftover debris, not spaghetti that is still growing. The part being printed right now, the grid box under the nozzle, has clean walls and is still stuck to the bed, and the temperatures are right on target. None of the allowed adjustments (fan, speed, flow, temperatures) can fix strands that are already lying on the bed, and nothing suggests one is needed. One thing I'm not sure about: I can't tell from the camera whether the small block is part of this job, for example a finished first stage. If it is still being printed, its surface is messy. That is why my confidence is medium, not high. If the strands start to grow or snag the nozzle, the next turn should pause the print for a person.
